# opencode-result A plugin for the [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) TUI (v2) that lets the agent hand you a result report when it finishes a task: a summary in markdown with links, notes and screenshots. Reports appear in the sidebar and open in a large window right in the terminal, images included. > Supports OpenCode V2 2.2.5 or newer. V1 is not supported.

The demo shows the Results section in the sidebar, the `/results` list, and a report window where `n` jumps between sections; the recording terminal draws images with blocks, while Kitty or Sixel terminals show them sharp, as below.

## Features - **Agent tools.** The agent publishes a report with `result_create` and adds to it later with `result_append`. A session can have several reports. - **Real images in the terminal.** Screenshots are drawn with Kitty graphics or Sixel, and with colored blocks where neither works. An image that is partly scrolled out is cropped, so it stays sharp and never spills over the window. - **Results in the sidebar.** Each report shows its status, image count and time. Click one to open it. - **Large report window.** It takes nearly the whole terminal (up to 220 columns). The content is on the left and a clickable table of contents, with headings and images, is on the right. - **`/results`** lists every report in the session, with search. - **A toast** appears when the agent publishes a new report. - **Reports stay.** They are saved in OpenCode's data directory, and every image is copied into the report, so temporary screenshots can be deleted.

## Requirements - OpenCode V2 2.2.5 or newer, on Windows, macOS or Linux. - For sharp images, a terminal with Kitty graphics or Sixel: for example kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty, foot, iTerm2, or Windows Terminal 1.22+. Other terminals show images as colored blocks. ## Install Install a release from GitHub with the OpenCode CLI. Pin the tag: a pinned install is cached and OpenCode can tell when a newer release exists. ```sh opencode plugin add github:igorovh/opencode-result#v0.2.0 ``` This adds the plugin to the global `plugins` array in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. Restart the TUI and a `Results` section appears in the session sidebar once the agent publishes its first report. You can also add the entry to the config yourself: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": ["github:igorovh/opencode-result#v0.2.0"] } ``` Update or remove it later: ```sh opencode plugin update github:igorovh/opencode-result#v0.2.0 opencode plugin remove github:igorovh/opencode-result#v0.2.0 ``` ## Agent tools | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `result_create` | New report: `title`, `markdown`, optional `status` (`success`, `partial`, `failed`, `info`) | | `result_append` | Adds markdown and images to an earlier report, or changes its title or status | | `result_list` | Lists the reports in the current session | Images use normal markdown, one per line: `![caption](path)`. A path can be absolute, relative to the session directory, start with `~`, or be a `file:`, `http(s):` or `data:` URL. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP up to 64 MiB are accepted. A missing or invalid image fails the call with a clear error, so the agent can fix it. Ask the agent for a report ("publish a result report when you're done"), or turn on `remind` (below) so it does so after every task. ## Keys and commands | Where | Key | Action | |---|---|---| | Sidebar | click a report | Open it | | Sidebar | click `Results` | Open the list | | Anywhere | `/results`, or `Show results` in the palette | Open the list of the session's reports | | Report | `↑` `↓` / `j` `k`, mouse wheel | Scroll | | Report | `space` `b` / `PgDn` `PgUp` | Scroll a page | | Report | `g` `G` / `Home` `End` | Top, bottom | | Report | `n` `p` / `→` `←` | Next or previous section | | Report | click an entry in the contents | Jump to it | | Report | click an image | Open it in the system image viewer | | Report | `o` | Open the report folder | | Report | `esc`, `q`, click outside | Close | `esc` takes you back where you came from: a report opened from the sidebar closes straight to the session, and a report opened from `/results` goes back to the list.

## Options Both options belong to the server part of the plugin, so set them on its entry in `opencode.jsonc`. `opencode plugin add` does not write options; add them by hand, using the same spec string: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "github:igorovh/opencode-result#v0.2.0", "options": { "remind": true, "dir": "~/reports" } } ] } ``` - `remind` (default `false`): adds a short system instruction to every request, asking the agent to publish a report when it finishes a task. It costs a few dozen tokens per request. - `dir`: where reports are stored. `~` is expanded and relative paths start at your home directory. The default is `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/result`, or `~/.local/share/opencode/result` when `XDG_DATA_HOME` is not set. The TUI part has no options, so nothing needs to go into `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`. ## How it works - **Storage.** Each report is a folder `///` with `report.json` and an `images/` folder. Reports from subagent sessions show up in their parent session too. - **Server and TUI.** The server part registers the agent tools and an RPC service. The TUI reads reports through that RPC, so it also works when OpenCode runs on another machine: images are then sent over RPC. - **Compiled TUI.** OpenCode does not run the Solid compiler on plugin files inside `node_modules`, where a `github:` install lives ([anomalyco/opencode#39986](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/39986)), so the repository ships the compiled `dist/tui.js`. - **Images.** They render with OpenTUI's ``: Kitty graphics, then Sixel, then colored Unicode blocks. While you scroll, images use blocks, which move smoothly, and switch to full quality once scrolling stops. Force a protocol with `OPENTUI_IMAGE_PROTOCOL=kitty|sixel|blocks`. Remote images are downloaded with a 20 s timeout and at most 5 redirects. - **The report window** is the plugin's own overlay rather than OpenCode's dialog, because the dialog is at most 116 columns wide. ## Development Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh). ```sh git clone https://github.com/igorovh/opencode-result.git cd opencode-result bun install bun test bun run typecheck bun run compile # rebuilds dist/tui.js; commit it with any change to src/tui.tsx bun run check:dist # dist/ may import only modules that OpenCode provides ``` To run your checkout instead of the published plugin, put its path in `plugins` and restart the TUI. After that, OpenCode reloads the plugin whenever a file changes. The TUI loads `dist/tui.js`, so run `bun run compile` after editing `src/tui.tsx`. ```jsonc { "plugins": ["/path/to/opencode-result"] } ``` ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
